portfolio.title: normcorp // Deterministic Legal Entity Normalizer & Blocking Engine
portfolio.summary: High-throughput, zero-dependency Python streaming engine and CLI that eliminates O(N^2) quadratic scaling bottlenecks in enterprise entity matching by deterministically normalizing corporate structures across 8 global jurisdictions and computing Soundex blocking keys.
portfolio.context: Enterprise data pipelines and CRM migrations (Salesforce, HubSpot, SAP) frequently struggle with messy corporate names. Probabilistic fuzzy matching (Levenshtein, Splink, Dedupe) triggers false-positive entity merges and explodes in quadratic compute complexity on unindexed datasets.
portfolio.objective: Build a lightweight, zero-dependency streaming CLI and library that standardizes international corporate suffixes, cleans punctuation noise, and calculates deterministic phonetic blocking keys in constant O(1) memory.
portfolio.role: Lead Author & Open-Source Maintainer — architected the jurisdictional regex lexer, Soundex phonetic generator, constant-memory streaming pipeline, automated GitHub Actions matrix CI, and PyPI packaging.
approach: Engineered a multi-jurisdiction priority lexer standardizing complex entity structures across US, UK, Singapore (ACRA), DACH (GmbH, AG, KG), Netherlands (BV, NV), France/Spain/Italy (SA, SRL, SAS, SPA), and Philippines (INC, CORP, OPC).
Implemented 4-character American Soundex phonetic blocking partitions and multi-tier substring prefix keys (Left 25, 15, 10) to support high-speed database joins and index blocking.
Built a streaming CLI supporting Unix pipes and constant O(1) memory iteration over multi-gigabyte files.
Integrated dynamic Excel formula injection via OpenPyXL to export production spreadsheets with native lookup helper columns.
deliverables: PEP 621 compliant Python library and CLI built with Hatchling.
Zero-dependency streaming I/O processor and optional OpenPyXL Excel export helper.
Comprehensive test suite (32 unit & integration tests, 94% coverage) and GitHub Actions CI matrix for Python 3.10-3.13.
portfolio.outcome: Processes 100,000 corporate records in 1.28 seconds with under 15 MB of memory, providing an open-source alternative to heavy probabilistic matching tools.

portfolio.title: tabula-guard // Tabular Schema Drift & PII Auditor for Pre-Commit
portfolio.summary: Zero-dependency Git pre-commit hook and CLI auditor that stops unmasked PII, schema drift, and null pollution before tabular datasets are committed to version control.
portfolio.context: Accidentally committing raw client data, CRM extracts, or analytics dumps containing unmasked PII triggers immediate legal and compliance breaches (GDPR, CCPA, Philippine Data Privacy Act), while silent schema drift corrupts downstream ETL jobs.
portfolio.objective: Build a fast, pre-commit-compatible auditor that blocks contaminated CSV/TSV commits using regex scanning, Luhn algorithm verification, and schema contract validation.
portfolio.role: Lead Developer & Security Architect — engineered the PII detection patterns, Luhn algorithm validator, schema comparison engine, pre-commit configuration, and matrix CI.
approach: Implemented high-precision PII detection for emails, phone numbers, and SSN/tax IDs, paired with Luhn algorithm checksums on credit cards to prevent false positives.
Built schema contract enforcement checking staged files against JSON baselines to catch column drift and unexpected schema mutations.
Engineered configurable null rate thresholds (flagging columns exceeding empty thresholds).
Packaged as a native pre-commit hook via .pre-commit-hooks.yaml with 90% automated test coverage in GitHub Actions.
deliverables: Python CLI and Git pre-commit hook package.
Luhn credit card and PII validation engine.
15 automated unit & integration tests and GitHub Actions CI matrix for Python 3.10-3.13.
portfolio.outcome: Blocks dirty or sensitive data commits with colored terminal diagnostics, ensuring organizational data privacy compliance prior to repository pushes.

portfolio.title: Contact Consolidator // Multi-Vector Deduplication & Merging Engine
portfolio.summary: High-performance Python data engine utilizing Disjoint Set Union (DSU) graph algorithms and priority conflict matrices to deduplicate, normalize, and merge massive B2B lead lists across heterogeneous spreadsheets.
portfolio.context: Enterprise CRM migrations routinely ingest customer contacts from dozens of disparate spreadsheets. Duplicates share conflicting partial identifiers (alternate emails, partial phones, LinkedIn profiles), causing naive deduplication to fail or explode in compute time.
portfolio.objective: Build an optimized graph clustering engine linking duplicates across 6 matching vectors simultaneously with deterministic conflict resolution via a 136-tier priority matrix.
portfolio.role: Lead Developer — designed the Disjoint Set Union (DSU) graph clustering architecture, priority score resolution engine, multi-sheet workbook parser, and unit test suite.
approach: Implemented Disjoint Set Union (DSU) with path compression for near-constant O(α(N)) cluster discovery across 6 identifiers.
Engineered a 136-tier Result Code priority matrix ensuring high-value interaction records prevail while backfilling demographic attributes.
Automated text normalization, E.164 phone sanitization, LinkedIn URL stripping, and DNC list enforcement.
Developed a 32-test unit testing suite covering scoring, validation, and multi-vector graph merging.
deliverables: Core DSU deduplication pipeline (consolidate.py).
Configurable column mapping and 136-tier priority matrix (config.json).
Comprehensive 32-test unit test suite (test_consolidate.py).
portfolio.outcome: Successfully deduplicates and prioritizes over 1,000,000 contact records in seconds with zero external database dependencies.

portfolio.role: Sole Author — designed both the Python batch CLI and the zero-dependency client-side HTML/JavaScript application.
approach: Engineered an 8-stage normalization pipeline standardizing dialer prefixes, splitting full names, and mapping geographic regions.
Integrated Google libphonenumber and Python phonenumbers for strict E.164 dialer formatting across multi-line priority queues.
Implemented automated substring matching against custom DNC exclusion lists to screen out unqualified job titles.
Built an in-browser web application using SheetJS for 100% private, local client-side processing.
deliverables: Python CLI data cleaner (contact_lot_cleaner.py).
Interactive browser-based web application (contact_lot_cleaner.html).
Customizable job title exclusion filter (excluded_titles.txt).

portfolio.title: EOC Buff // End of Campaign Report Generator
portfolio.status: In Production at G9 Outsourcing Corp.
portfolio.summary: Full-stack client/server operational utility that ingests campaign data from Google Sheets via an authenticated local Python CORS proxy and renders styled Excel summaries with zero manual formula entry.
portfolio.context: Campaign reporting teams had to manually copy, reformat, and calculate performance metrics from live Google Sheets into client-facing Excel spreadsheets, risking human error and spending hours per reporting cycle.
portfolio.objective: Build a secure, lightweight, and self-contained reporting application that automatically pulls data, runs aggregation logic, and outputs formatted Excel reports.
portfolio.role: Lead Developer & Systems Architect — designed the architecture, wrote the Python proxy server, and engineered the browser-based data processing UI.
approach: Engineered a lightweight local HTTP proxy in Python (`server.py`) using `http.server` and `urllib.request` with domain-filtering safeguards (restricting requests strictly to `docs.google.com`) to bypass browser CORS constraints.

Built an interactive single-page application (`EOC_Report_Generator.html`) incorporating SheetJS (`xlsx`) and ExcelJS to read, normalize, and construct customized workbook layouts with embedded styles.
Implemented clean command-line logging and real-time frontend status feedback for report generation progress.
deliverables: Python HTTP proxy server with domain validation security.
Interactive browser-based report generator with SheetJS & ExcelJS processing.
Direct one-click export of styled Excel workbooks.
portfolio.outcome: Eliminated manual spreadsheet transcription errors and streamlined campaign wrap-up reporting into an automated workflow executable with a single command (`python server.py`).

portfolio.title: ShelfIQ // Perishable Spoilage Prediction & Restock Decision System
portfolio.summary: Multi-engine Streamlit machine learning application that predicts cold-chain perishable spoilage risks and generates automated rescue-pricing actions for Philippine grocery MSMEs.
portfolio.context: Mid-sized grocers and chilled-goods distributors face significant revenue loss during El Niño heat waves and cold-chain transit delays because standard static inventory models cannot anticipate transit decay.
portfolio.objective: Build an end-to-end ML decision support application forecasting Remaining Useful Life (RUL) and triggering timely discount strategies before goods spoil.
portfolio.role: Machine Learning Engineer (Capstone Co-Developer) — developed the Spoilage Prediction Engine (pages/rul_model.py) using Random Forest classification, mapped feature importances, and built automated urgency-tier markdown rules.
approach: Trained a Random Forest Classifier on historical inventory logs and transit metrics (stock levels, days to sell, daily demand, lead times, sensitivity scores) to predict perishable batch spoilage.

Engineered dynamic inference comparing current inventory lots against remaining shelf-life days to segment stock into four action tiers (Final Markdown <24h, Priority Sell 1-2d, Early Markdown 3-5d, Watch 5+d).
Implemented automated rescue interventions including upcycle recommendations for produce/dairy and targeted discount ranges (5% to 50%) to accelerate demand prior to spoilage.
Integrated prediction outputs directly into the shared Streamlit application with interactive KPI metrics and downloadable CSV reports.
deliverables: Random Forest Remaining Useful Life (RUL) Spoilage Engine (pages/rul_model.py).
Dynamic urgency tier categorization and markdown rule generator.
Interactive Streamlit dashboard metrics and downloadable CSV reports.
portfolio.outcome: Successfully pitched and demonstrated to Uplift Code Camp evaluators as an end-to-end decision support tool bridging data science predictions with actionable store-level retail decisions.

portfolio.title: Match Link // Company Name Templater
portfolio.summary: Production-hardened FastAPI and Pandas web utility that normalizes corporate legal suffixes, strips non-alphanumeric noise, and dynamically generates tiered Excel lookup formulas with bounded memory caching, Docker containerization, and 94% automated test coverage.
portfolio.context: Reconciling vendor, client, and lead lists across CRM platforms and accounting databases frequently fails exact matching due to inconsistent entity spellings (e.g., 'PTE. LTD.', 'LLC', 'Corp') and punctuation differences.
portfolio.objective: Create a fast, standalone desktop/browser application to ingest tabular data, automate legal suffix stripping, and calculate live Excel formula helper columns for multi-tiered lookup matching.
portfolio.role: Lead Developer & Maintainer — designed the FastAPI backend, normalization regex pipelines, OpenPyXL workbook formatting, and glassmorphism interface.
approach: Engineered suffix-normalization regular expressions mapping varied legal forms (P.T.E. L.T.D., PRIVATE LIMITED, etc.) to canonical tokens before stripping them down to alphanumeric match keys.
Calculated 1-based dynamic Excel column indices to generate formula strings (=LEFT(ColRow, N)) directly inside exported workbooks.
Constructed an asynchronous FastAPI backend paired with an accessible drag-and-drop and text-paste frontend.
Hardened server reliability with BoundedResultStore LRU/TTL caching to prevent memory exhaustion and implemented GitHub Actions matrix CI across Python 3.10-3.13.
deliverables: FastAPI backend with bounded in-memory LRU/TTL result storage.
Multi-stage Dockerfile and docker-compose deployment configuration.
30-case automated Pytest suite (94% coverage) with GitHub Actions CI matrix.
portfolio.outcome: Automated data-preparation tasks for list reconciliation, eliminating manual text-editing hours and standardizing lookup keys across operational databases.
